Exactness
Every measure is defined as an exact value of Core's exact geometry (Core §
) and rounded at most once, to an integer, with

An evaluator MUST compute every measure exactly as its definition states, rounding only where and as the definition says.
The room of an element
An extension element is in at most one room, decided from its core members alone, as the official extensions decide it (FS_electrical §6.1):
an element with a
host is in the host's room;
an element with a
host is in the room anchored in the face (Core §
) on the host's side of the wall: on side
, the face to the left of the wall's location line walked from its start to its end; on side
, the face to its right — or in no room, when no room is anchored in that face;
an element with a
host is in the room anchored in the bounded face that contains the host's
, or in no room when the position is on a location line or in no bounded face with a room;
an element without a host is in no room.
An evaluator MUST decide the room of every extension element exactly as this section defines it.
Members of extension elements and records
Some measures and arguments read an extension's own members — an element's, or a record's such as a circuit (FS_electrical §3.1). A member is read
with its default

What each measure reads

Each measure's definition says what it reads besides Core: "reads FS_electrical" means that every use of the measure reads that extension, and "with a match, reads the extension" means that only a use with a
argument does. A measure that says neither reads only Core and the core members of extension elements (Core §
), and is evaluated for every valid document.
